gen.title: Formal definition with constants c and k

cards.stem: Which pair of constants is required in the formal definition to establish the bound?
cards.quote: Formal Definition: f(n) = O(g(n)) means there are positive constants c and k, such that 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ cg(n) for all n ≥ k.

cards.stem: Which inequality correctly expresses the upper bound in the formal definition?
options: f(n) ≥ cg(n) for all n ≥ k
cards.quote: there are positive constants c and k, such that 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ cg(n) for all n ≥ k.

cards.stem: For which values of n must the bounding inequality hold in the formal definition?
options: for some n less than k
cards.quote: Formal Definition: f(n) = O(g(n)) means there are positive constants c and k, such that 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ cg(n) for all n ≥ k.

cards.stem: What must be true about the constants c and k with respect to n?
options: must equal n for all n ≥ k
cards.quote: The values of c and k must be fixed for the function f and must not depend on n.
